case_name: Century Campus Housing Management, L.P. v. Elda Hana, LLC

issues.label: Court's Rule 41(b) authority
issues.why: The court must confirm it had authority under HRCP 41(b) to dismiss a counterclaim for failure to prosecute.

issues.label: Proper procedural vehicle used
issues.why: The court must ensure dismissal was properly sought by motion (not sua sponte) and that HRCP 41(b) standards apply to the posture of the case.

issues.label: Counterclaim vs complaint treatment
issues.why: The court must consider whether any different considerations apply when dismissing a counterclaim rather than an initial complaint.

issues.label: Who bore prosecution duty
issues.why: The court must determine whether EH/KAD had the obligation to move the counterclaim forward and what actions were required.

issues.label: What counts as inaction
issues.why: The court must identify what qualifies as prosecutorial activity (discovery, motions, trial setting, status conferences, etc.) and whether EH/KAD did none.

issues.label: Length of delay measurement
issues.why: The court must define the relevant time period (from March 5, 2020 or other date) and calculate the actual period of inactivity.

issues.label: Effect of remand posture
issues.why: The court must account for the post-remand procedural posture and whether remand required any specific steps or scheduling by the court.

issues.label: Impact of court-controlled scheduling
issues.why: The court must consider whether the lack of a trial date/status conference or scheduling order contributed to inactivity and how that affects Rule 41(b).

issues.label: Pandemic-related disruptions
issues.why: The court must consider whether COVID-era court disruptions reasonably explain delay or reduce culpability for inactivity.

issues.label: Notice of risk of dismissal
issues.why: The court must decide whether EH/KAD had adequate notice that failure to act could result in dismissal with prejudice.

issues.label: Opportunity to be heard
issues.why: The court must ensure due process was satisfied when submitting the motion without a hearing and deciding on briefs only.

issues.label: Compliance with HRCP 7/briefing rules
issues.why: The court must verify that the motion, opposition, and supporting materials complied with applicable briefing and service requirements.

issues.label: Adequacy of Century's showing
issues.why: The court must assess whether Century met its burden to justify dismissal beyond conclusory assertions of inactivity.

issues.label: Specificity of court findings
issues.why: The court must consider whether the dismissal order needed explicit findings (delay, willfulness, prejudice, alternatives) to permit review.

issues.label: Use of minute order reasoning
issues.why: The court must determine whether incorporating a minute order by reference provides sufficient legal reasoning and factual basis.

issues.label: Discrepancy: 'arguments of counsel'
issues.why: The court must address whether stating it considered 'arguments of counsel' is accurate or problematic where no hearing occurred.

issues.label: Standard of culpability required
issues.why: The court must decide whether Rule 41(b) dismissal required willful or contumacious conduct versus mere negligence.

issues.label: Consideration of lesser sanctions
issues.why: Before dismissing with prejudice, the court must consider and explain why lesser sanctions would be inadequate.

issues.label: With-prejudice proportionality
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether dismissal with prejudice was proportionate to the delay and circumstances.

issues.label: Prejudice to Century assessment
issues.why: The court must determine whether Century suffered actual prejudice (stale evidence, costs, uncertainty) from the delay.

issues.label: Presumed prejudice doctrine
issues.why: The court must consider whether prejudice may be presumed from prolonged delay under Hawaiʻi law and whether rebutted.

issues.label: Balancing public policy factors
issues.why: The court must balance docket management and expeditious resolution against the policy favoring decisions on the merits.

issues.label: Client vs counsel responsibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether inactivity is attributable to counsel changes/withdrawals and how that affects sanction severity.

issues.label: Effect of counsel appearances/withdrawals
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the few notices of appearance/withdrawal constitute activity or explain delay.

issues.label: Requirement of warning/conditional order
issues.why: The court must consider whether a prior warning, order to show cause, or conditional dismissal should have preceded dismissal with prejudice.

issues.label: Record support for 'no action'
issues.why: The court must confirm the docket supports the finding that EH/KAD took no action for nearly four years.

issues.label: Defining 'prosecute' for counterclaim
issues.why: The court must determine what affirmative steps are expected to prosecute a counterclaim absent court deadlines.

issues.label: Pretrial statement duty
issues.why: The court must decide whether failure to file a pretrial statement was required at that stage and whether any deadline existed.

issues.label: Discovery not mandatory consideration
issues.why: The court must assess whether the absence of propounded discovery necessarily indicates failure to prosecute.

issues.label: Effect of settlement discussions
issues.why: The court must consider whether any off-docket settlement negotiations or agreed stays explain inactivity.

issues.label: Any stipulations or stays
issues.why: The court must determine whether the parties agreed to pause proceedings or whether any stay was in effect.

issues.label: Concurrent proceedings elsewhere
issues.why: The court must consider whether related litigation, appeals, bankruptcy, or administrative proceedings justified delay.

issues.label: Judicial assignment changes impact
issues.why: The court must assess whether changes in presiding judges affected case management or contributed to delay.

issues.label: Proper exercise of discretion
issues.why: The court must ensure the decision reflects a reasoned exercise of discretion rather than a mechanical time-based dismissal.

issues.label: Correct legal standard applied
issues.why: The court must apply Hawaiʻi appellate precedent governing HRCP 41(b) dismissals and not an incorrect or incomplete test.

issues.label: Consideration of EH/KAD explanations
issues.why: The court must address any reasons or excuses presented in opposition and whether they mitigate against dismissal.

issues.label: Evidentiary basis for opposition
issues.why: The court must assess whether EH/KAD supported its opposition with admissible evidence/affidavits and what weight to give it.

issues.label: Burden allocation on motion
issues.why: The court must determine who bears the burden of proving lack of prosecution and/or justification for dismissal with prejudice.

issues.label: Requirement of prejudice finding
issues.why: The court must decide whether a specific finding of prejudice is required under Hawaiʻi law for Rule 41(b) dismissal with prejudice.

issues.label: Consideration of delay length alone
issues.why: The court must decide whether delay duration alone is sufficient or whether additional factors must be shown.

issues.label: Effect of court's no-hearing order
issues.why: The court must ensure the decision to submit without hearing complied with applicable rules and did not deny meaningful opportunity to respond.

issues.label: Adequacy of service via JEFS
issues.why: The court must confirm electronic service was effective and that parties received notice and deadlines.

issues.label: Timeliness of written order entry
issues.why: The court must consider whether the long gap between minute order (Apr 2024) and written order (Jan 2025) affects validity or appellate rights.

issues.label: Operative date of dismissal
issues.why: The court must determine whether dismissal took effect at the minute order or only upon entry of the written order for purposes of deadlines.

issues.label: Finality and appealability
issues.why: The court must determine whether the dismissal order was final or interlocutory and whether final judgment properly entered later.

issues.label: Scope: dismissal of only counterclaim
issues.why: The court must ensure the order correctly specifies what claims are dismissed and whether any claims remained pending.

issues.label: Res judicata effect of dismissal
issues.why: The court must understand that a with-prejudice dismissal operates as an adjudication on the merits and ensure that consequence is warranted.

issues.label: Rule 41(b) 'adjudication' exceptions
issues.why: The court must consider whether any Rule 41(b) exceptions apply that would make dismissal without prejudice.

issues.label: Consideration of equitable factors
issues.why: The court must evaluate equities such as hardship, reliance, and fairness before imposing the harsh sanction of dismissal with prejudice.

issues.label: Alternative case-management tools
issues.why: The court must consider whether orders setting deadlines, status conferences, or sanctions would serve the same purpose without dismissal.

issues.label: Due process for sanctions severity
issues.why: Because dismissal with prejudice is a severe sanction, the court must ensure heightened due process and careful reasoning.

issues.label: Consistency with local rules
issues.why: The court must confirm compliance with any circuit/local rules on case inactivity, dismissal calendars, or pretrial requirements.

issues.label: Inherent powers vs Rule 41(b)
issues.why: The court must distinguish dismissal under Rule 41(b) from inherent-power sanctions and apply the correct framework.

issues.label: Adequate record for appellate review
issues.why: The court must create a record explaining the rationale so an appellate court can review for abuse of discretion.

issues.label: Motion for reconsideration standard
issues.why: On reconsideration, the court must apply the proper standard (new evidence, change in law, clear error) and address the grounds raised.

issues.label: Preservation of issues for appeal
issues.why: The court must consider whether EH/KAD preserved objections (e.g., no hearing, lack of findings) through opposition and reconsideration.

issues.label: Effect of delay on evidence
issues.why: The court must consider whether witness availability, document retention, or memory degradation supports prejudice or sanctions.

issues.label: Good-cause determination
issues.why: The court must determine whether 'good cause' existed for dismissal as stated in the order and what facts support it.

issues.label: Accuracy of factual premises
issues.why: The court must verify factual assertions such as '46 months' and 'close to four years' and ensure they match the docket.

issues.label: Consideration of partial dismissal
issues.why: The court must consider whether some counterclaim counts could proceed or be dismissed without prejudice rather than total with-prejudice dismissal.

issues.label: Effect on compulsory counterclaims
issues.why: If the counterclaim was compulsory, dismissal with prejudice may bar future litigation, increasing the need for careful sanction analysis.

issues.label: Any prior court warnings or orders
issues.why: The court must review whether any prior orders directed action or warned of dismissal, which affects appropriateness of the sanction.
